result.title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting
result.summary: Recent time series foundation models (TSFMs) can consume covariates in-context, extending zero-shot forecasting to problems driven by external factors. This enables scenario analysis: forecasting how a target responds to events that set covariates to chosen future values. Whether they can do this reliably is an open question. We introduce WhatIf-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well forecasters use covariates to forecast a target's response to future events. WhatIf-Bench is semi-synthetic: time series come from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks, with controlled covariate-target relationships grounded in each system. Each task presents a history of events intervening on covariates, then asks to forecast a future event that either replays seen values (Replay) or sets them to unseen ones (Novel). Varying the number of covariates, historical events, and event length yields 37,665 tasks. Evaluating TSFMs, frontier LLMs, and simple regression baselines, we find the LLMs reach the highest skill (improvement over a naive baseline), ahead of the best TSFMs. Every model forecasts well on Replay futures (48 to 85% skill) but drops to -7 to 50% on Novel futures, with the regression baselines falling the most. Skill on Novel futures also falls as events set more covariates jointly. More historical events raise skill on Novel futures across the board, but large differences remain. WhatIf-Bench reveals generalization to Novel futures as the core challenge, and offers a testbed toward arbitrary scenario analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 WhatIf-Bench：以数据中心、电网、交通与供水系统的半合成时间序列，评测预测模型能否依据历史干预事件预测目标对未来事件（复现已见取值 Replay 或使用未见取值 Novel）的响应，并比较 TSFM、LLM 与回归基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「模型是否真正使用外部证据、以及在未见干预取值与更多事件同时设置时泛化」的诊断设计，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据是否被实际使用、组合与场景泛化的评价方式提供参照，属远领域线索，尚需核查，未见与视觉 latent 推理的直接联系。
